entries.sanskrit:
चतुर्थे बन्धु-निधनं श्रुत्वात्म-ज्ञान-लब्धये ।

उद्धवस्योपदेशेन क्षता मैत्रेयम् आगमत् ॥

तैर् ब्राह्मणैर् अनुज्ञाताः । वारुणीं पैष्ठीं मदिराम् ॥१॥
word_for_word: for attaining knowledge of the self
entries.literal_english: In the Fourth Canto, after hearing of the death of his relatives, Vidura went to Maitreya for knowledge of the self, following Uddhava’s instruction. He was permitted by the brāhmaṇas and accepted the Varuṇī liquor.

entries.sanskrit: वारुण्य् एव मैत्रेयं तस्य दोषेण निम्लोचति अस्तं गच्छति सति । मर्दनं कदनम् ॥२॥
entries.literal_english: The Varuṇī itself caused Maitreya distress when the sun was setting; this is the explanation of the affliction mentioned in the verse.

entries.literal_english: He approached the Sarasvatī and performed ācamana, sipping water for purification.

entries.literal_english: ‘I too was spoken to earlier, in Dvārakā.’

word_for_word: without a house and without a support
entries.literal_english: He made a sign and established a dwelling, yet remained without a house and without a worldly support.

entries.sanskrit: विरजं विरजसं शुद्ध-सत्त्व-मयम् । विदितं लक्षितम् । कौशं कौशेयम् ॥७॥
entries.literal_english: The form is stainless, free from passion and made of pure sattva; it is perceived as a silken form.

entries.sanskrit: अधिश्रित्योपरि स्थापयित्वा । अपाश्रितः पृष्ठतोऽवष्टब्धोऽर्भको बालः कोमलोऽश्वत्थो येन तम् । त्यक्तं पिप्पलं विषय-सुखं येन तम् । तथाप्य् अकृशम् आनन्द-पूर्णम् ॥८॥
word_for_word: a tender young child like a delicate aśvattha tree
by whom the pipal of sense pleasure was abandoned
nevertheless not thin, but full of bliss
entries.literal_english: Having mounted and placed Himself above, He was supported from behind like a tender young child or delicate aśvattha tree. He had abandoned the pipal tree of sense pleasure, yet He was not diminished; He was full of bliss.

entries.sanskrit: द्वैपायनः सुहृत् सखा च यस्य स स्व-गुरु-पुत्रत्वात्, पराशर-शिष्यो मैत्रेय इत्य् अर्थः ॥९॥
word_for_word: whose friend and companion was Dvaipāyana
because he was the son of his own teacher
entries.literal_english: Dvaipāyana was his friend and companion because he was the son of his own teacher; Maitreya was the disciple of Parāśara. That is the meaning.

entries.sanskrit: प्रमोदेन भावेन चानता कन्धरा यस्य । पठान्तरे प्रमोदस्य भारेण । अनुरागेण सह हासो यस्यां तया समीक्षया विश्रमयन् विगत-श्रमं कुर्वन् ॥१०॥
word_for_word: according to another reading, by the weight of joy
by that glance He gave rest
entries.literal_english: His neck was bent with joyful feeling, or, according to another reading, under the weight of joy. His glance contained laughter together with affection; by that glance He gave them rest and removed their fatigue.

entries.sanskrit: हे उद्धव, ते मनसीप्सितम् अहम् अन्तः-स्थितो वेद वेद्मि । दाने हेतुः---विश्व-सृजां वसूनां च मिलितानां सत्रे । हे वसो ! इति पुरा पूर्व-जन्मनि त्वं वसुर् अभूः, तदा मत्-प्राप्ति-कामेन त्वयाहम् इष्टः । अतस् तत्-साधनं ददामि दास्यामि । अन्यैर् मत्-पराङ्मुखैर् दुष्प्रापम् ॥११॥
word_for_word: what is desired in your mind
at the sacrifice of the gathered creators and Vasus
in a former birth you were a Vasu
you worshipped Me desiring to attain Me
I give the means for that attainment
difficult to obtain for others turned away from Me
entries.literal_english: ‘O Uddhava, I know what is desired in your mind, dwelling within you.’ The reason for the gift is this: at the sacrifice of the gathered creators and Vasus, Uddhava had been a Vasu in a former birth and had worshipped Kṛṣṇa desiring to attain Him. Kṛṣṇa therefore gives him the means for that attainment, which is difficult for those turned away from Him.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: तस्य भाग्यम् अभिनन्दति । स एष भवो जन्म ते भवानां मध्ये चरमः । यद्य् अस्मिन् मद्-अनुग्रह आसादितो लब्धः । यत् पुनर् मां रह एकान्ते विशदानुवृत्त्या एकान्त-भक्त्या ददृश्वान् दृष्टवान् असि एतद् दिष्ट्या भद्रं जातम् इत्य् अर्थः । नृ-लोकान् नृ-शब्देन जीवास् तेषां लोकान् उत्सृजन्तं वैकुण्ठं गच्छन्तम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥१२॥
word_for_word: is the last among your births
by good fortune this auspicious thing has occurred
leaving the human worlds and going to Vaikuṇṭha
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara praises Uddhava’s fortune. This is the last of his births, and he has obtained Kṛṣṇa’s mercy: through pure, exclusive devotion he has seen Kṛṣṇa in a secluded place. By good fortune this auspicious event has occurred; he is leaving the human worlds and going to Vaikuṇṭha.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: ददामीति यद् उक्तं, तद् एव निर्दिशति । पुरा पूर्वस्मिन् पाद्मे कल्पे । आदि-सर्गे सर्गोपक्रमे । मम महिमा लीला अवभास्यते येन तत् ॥१३॥
word_for_word: formerly, in the previous Pādma Kalpa
by which My glory and play are manifested
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara identifies what Kṛṣṇa meant by saying ‘I give’. Formerly, in the previous Pādma Kalpa, at the beginning of creation, Kṛṣṇa’s glory and play were manifested through this teaching.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: इत्य् एवम् आदृतश् चासाव् उक्तश् चाहम् । प्रतीक्षणं कृपावलोक एवानुग्रहस् तस्य भाजनः पात्र-भूतः । पाठान्तरे प्रतिक्षणम् अनुग्रहस्य पात्रम् इति । शुचोऽश्रूणि मुञ्चन्न् आवभाषे उक्तवान् असि ॥१४॥
word_for_word: a compassionate glance at every moment
according to another reading, a recipient of mercy at every moment
entries.literal_english: Thus Kṛṣṇa honoured and addressed him. Uddhava was the recipient of mercy through a compassionate glance at every moment—or, according to another reading, he was continually a recipient of mercy. Releasing tears of sorrow, he spoke.

entries.sanskrit: न हि स्वाज्ञान-निवृत्ति-मात्र-कामोऽहं, किन्तु त्वन्-निषेवणोत्सुकस् त्वयि चाघटमानाचरणं दृष्ट्वा मे मोहो भवति, अतस् त्वं तत्त्व-ज्ञानं देहीति प्रार्थयितुम् आह---को न्व् इति । चतुर्षु धर्मादिषु तथापि, हे भूमन् ! भवत्-पदाम्भोज-निषेवणोत्सुकोऽहम्, तान् न प्रवृणोमि ॥१५॥
word_for_word: I do not merely desire the removal of my own ignorance
I am eager to serve You
among the four aims beginning with dharma
I am eager to serve Your lotus feet
entries.literal_english: I do not merely desire the removal of my own ignorance; I am eager to serve You. When I see conduct that seems impossible for You, I become bewildered, so I ask You to give me knowledge of the truth. O all-pervading Lord, although the four aims beginning with dharma are available, I do not choose them; I am eager only to serve Your lotus feet.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: अघटमानाचरणं दर्शयति । कर्माण्य् अनीहस्य निःस्पृहस्य निष्क्रियस्य वा । अभवस्य अजन्मनः भवो जन्म । कालात्मनस् तव अरि-भयाद् दुर्गाश्रयः पलायनं च। स्वात्मनि रतिर् यस्य तस्य बह्वीभिः स्त्रीभिर् गृहस्थाश्रम इति यद् इहास्मिन् विषये विदुषाम् अपि धीः संशयेन खिद्यति ॥१६॥
word_for_word: actions of one without desire, without longing, or inactive
for You, Time Himself, fleeing to a fort from fear of enemies
whose delight is in His own self
the household state with many women
even the intellect of the learned is troubled by doubt
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara explains the conduct that appears impossible: actions by One without desire, the birth of the Unborn, and, though He is Time Himself, fleeing to a fort from fear of enemies. Though delighting in His own self, He entered household life with many women. Even the intellect of learned people is troubled by doubt about this.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, मन्त्रेषु च प्रस्तुतेषु च सत्स्य् माम् आहूय वै अहो पृच्छेर् अपृच्छः । अकुण्ठितः कालादिना अखण्डः सन्ततः सदात्मा संशयादि-रहितो बोधो विद्या-शक्तिर् यस्य । मुग्धवद् अज्ञवत् । अप्रमत्तोऽवहितः सन् ॥१७॥
word_for_word: when the mantras and rites were being presented
unhindered by time and the like
unbroken, continuous and true in nature
whose knowledge is the power of wisdom
entries.literal_english: When the mantras and rites were being presented, You summoned me and asked me—‘Ah, you asked me.’ Your knowledge is unhindered by time, unbroken, continuous and true in nature, yet You acted like an innocent ignorant person while remaining attentive and alert.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: स्वात्मनस् तव रहो रहस्यं तत्त्वं तस्य प्रकाशकम् । कस्मै ब्रह्मणे । सर्वनामत्वम् आर्षम् । नोऽस्माकं ग्रहणायापि क्षमं यदि योग्यं, तर्हि वद । भर्तः स्वामिन्, यद् यतो वृजिनं सम्षार-दुःखम् अञ्जसानायासेन तरिष्यामः ॥१८॥
word_for_word: the secret truth of Your own self
the universal pronoun is an archaic usage
if it is suitable, then speak
the suffering of saṃsāra, which is misery
entries.literal_english: Tell us the secret truth of Your own self, which You revealed to Brahmā. The universal pronoun is an archaic usage. If this teaching is fit even for our understanding, then speak, O Lord, O Master, so that we may easily cross the suffering of saṃsāra.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: आवेदितो हार्दो हृदि-स्थितोऽभिप्रायो येन तस्मै ॥१९॥
word_for_word: the heartfelt intention was made known
which was present in the heart
to him by whom it was made known
entries.literal_english: The teaching was given to the one by whom the intention present in the heart was understood and made known.

entries.sanskrit: आराधित-पादो भगवान् स एव तीर्थं गुरुस् तस्माद् अधीतोऽधिगतस् तत्त्वात्म-विबोधस्य परमार्थात्म-ज्ञानस्य मार्गो येन सोऽहम् । देवं परिवृत्य प्रदक्षिणी-कृत्य॥२०॥
word_for_word: Bhagavān whose feet have been worshipped
He Himself is the sacred ford and the guru
from Him it was studied and understood
the path to knowledge of the self and ultimate reality
entries.literal_english: Bhagavān whose feet have been worshipped is Himself the sacred ford and the guru. From Him Uddhava learned and understood the path to knowledge of the self and ultimate reality, and he circumambulated the Lord.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: तस्त दर्शनेनाह्लादो वियोगेनार्तिश् च ताभ्यां युतो बदर्य्-आश्रम-स्थानं गमिष्यामि ॥२१॥
word_for_word: I shall go to the place of Badarī Āśrama
entries.literal_english: I am endowed both with joy from seeing Him and pain from separation; with these two feelings I shall go to Badarī Āśrama.

entries.sanskrit: मृदु परोपद्रव-शून्यम् । तीव्रं दुश्चरम् । दीर्घम् आकल्पान्तम् । तेपाते तपश् चरत इत्य् अर्थः । लोक-भावनौ लोकानुग्रह-कारकौ ॥२२॥
word_for_word: long, lasting until the end of the kalpa
causing the welfare of the worlds
entries.literal_english: Their austerity was gentle and free from harming others, yet severe and difficult to perform, and long-lasting until the end of the kalpa. They performed it as benefactors of the worlds, bringing welfare to the worlds.

entries.literal_english: Through knowledge and discrimination.

entries.sanskrit: विश्रम्भाद् विश्वासात् ॥२४॥
entries.literal_english: Through trust and confidence.

entries.sanskrit: यद् यस्माद् विष्णोर् भृत्याः स्व-भृत्य-प्रयोजन-साधकाः सन्तश् चरन्ति । न हि कृतार्थानाम् अन्यत् कृत्यम् अस्तीत्य् अर्थः ॥२५॥
word_for_word: move about accomplishing the purpose of His servants
न हि कृत-अर्थानाम् अन्यत् कृत्यम् अस्ति
for those whose purpose is fulfilled there is no other duty
entries.literal_english: The servants of Viṣṇu move about accomplishing the purpose of His servants. For those whose purpose is fulfilled there is no other duty; that is the meaning.

entries.sanskrit: तत्त्वाय संराध्य इति । अयं भावः---भगवतैव स्मरण-मात्रेण तवापि तत्त्वम् उपदिष्ट-प्रायम् । अथ केवलम् असम्भावनादि-निवृत्तये ज्ञानी कश्चिद् आराध्यः । स च तवाराध्यो मैत्रेयो न त्व् अहम् । ममान्तिक एव त्वद्-उपदेशे तस्यादिष्टत्वाद् इति ॥२६॥
word_for_word: the truth has almost been taught to you
for removing doubt and the like
Maitreya is the one you should worship
मम अन्तिके एव त्वत्-उपदेशे तस्य आदिष्टत्वात्
because he was appointed to instruct you near me
entries.literal_english: The idea is this: by merely remembering Bhagavān, the truth has almost been taught to you. To remove doubt and similar obstacles, a knower should be worshipped. Maitreya, not I, is the one you should worship, because he was appointed to instruct you in my presence.

entries.sanskrit: ब्रह्म-शापेननिधनं प्राप्तेषु यद्य् अस्मात् त्रयाणां ब्रह्मादीनाम् ईशो हरिर् अप्य् आकृतिंमनुष्याकारं त्यक्तवान् ॥२८॥
word_for_word: when death had been reached through Brahmā’s curse
although Hari is the Lord of the three beginning with Brahmā
entries.literal_english: When death came through the curse of Brahmā, Hari—Lord of the three beginning with Brahmā—also abandoned His human form.

entries.sanskrit: ब्रह्म-शापः अपदेशो मिषं यस्य तेन कालेन स्व-शक्ति-रूपेण । अमोघं वाञ्छितं यस्य । न ह्य् अत्र शापः प्रभुः, किन्तु भगवद्-इच्छैवेत्य् अर्थः ॥२९॥
word_for_word: for whom Brahmā’s curse was a pretext
through that time in the form of His own power
the curse is not the governing cause here
entries.literal_english: Brahmā’s curse was only a pretext; the actual instrument was time in the form of Bhagavān’s own power. His desire is unfailing. The curse is not the governing cause here—Bhagavān’s will alone is.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: मय्य् उपरते सति ज्ञानम् अर्हति ज्ञान-योग्यो भवति ॥३०॥
entries.literal_english: When I have ceased, he becomes fit for knowledge and qualified for wisdom.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: मत्तः सकाशाद् ईषद् अपि न्यूनो न भवति । यद्य् अस्माद् गुणैर् विषयैर् न क्षोभितः । मद्-वयुनं मद्-विषयं ज्ञानं लोकस्योपदिशन् ॥३१॥
word_for_word: मत्तः सकाशात् ईषत् अपि न्यूनः न भवति
he is not even slightly less than Me
not agitated by qualities or objects
knowledge concerning Me and My object
entries.literal_english: He is not even slightly less than Me, and is not agitated by qualities or objects. He teaches the world knowledge concerning Me and My object.

entries.sanskrit: एवम् अनेनाभिप्रायेण शब्द-योनिना वेद-कर्त्रा ईजे पूजयामास ॥३२॥
word_for_word: by the source of sound, the maker of the Veda
entries.literal_english: With this intention, Brahmā, the maker of the Veda and source of sacred sound, worshipped Bhagavān.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and glossed.

entries.sanskrit: अन्येषां पशु-तुल्यानाम् । विक्लवात्मनाम् अधीर-चित्तानाम् ॥ मनसेक्षितं चिन्तितम् ॥३३-३५॥
word_for_word: of those with agitated, unsteady minds
perceived and conceived by the mind
entries.literal_english: For others who are like animals, with agitated and unsteady minds, the matter is only mentally perceived and conceived.

entries.sanskrit: कालिन्द्याः सकाशात् सिद्ध एव विदुरः कतिपयैर् दिनैः स्वः-सरितं गङ्गां प्रापद्यत प्राप्तः ॥३६॥
word_for_word: reached the heavenly river, the Gaṅgā
entries.literal_english: Vidura, already perfected, reached the heavenly river Gaṅgā from the Yamunā after a few days.
